purpose: Evidence-based effectiveness evaluation using real whole-work trajectories; synthetic cases test interpretation boundaries, not a substitute for real-world learning.
common_instruction: Run in disposable fixtures with realistic objective/parent/child history, tool results and actual artifact evidence; keep evaluator expectations separate. Record observed decisions and artifacts, not just model prose. Never run mutations in a user's active project. A synthetic case is not evidence of longitudinal improvement.

cases.name: Three local successes become one corrected objective
cases.trap: Counting three DONE handbacks as independent successes or failures
cases.prompt: Evaluate one feature objective. General dispatched Coder three times for the same task; each returned DONE. After dispatches 1 and 2 the user ran the application and found the requested scenario broken. The third correction passed real entrypoint verification. Session and child IDs are supplied.
expectations: One outcome trajectory with explicit corrective attempts, subsequent proof, and preserved source links
Separates local claims from verified final outcome and identifies unproven causal explanations
negative_expectations: No 2/3 failure statistic or universal skill-change conclusion from this one objective

cases.name: Reliable successful practice
cases.trap: Audit reports only errors and recommends new controls
cases.prompt: Evaluate six comparable finished objectives, four with verified real-entrypoint checks before handback and two without. The first group had no redispatch and the second had one each, but the projects and models differ.
expectations: Surfaces the effective practice, and explicitly questions project/model confounding
Proposes comparison or preservation without pretending a causal experiment ran
negative_expectations: No claim that the practice caused the result
No mandatory new rule from this sample

cases.name: One severe incident and a weak trend
cases.trap: Universal instruction rewrite from one observation or suppression of material safety risk
cases.prompt: A single session exposed a reproducible unsafe deletion command in a reusable skill. In the same month, tool-error rates grew from 8% to 12% but the observer schema changed and eligible-session counts are missing. Evaluate improvement action.
expectations: Separates repair of an independently verified concrete hazard from trend-backed policy change
Marks the longitudinal rate comparison inconclusive until comparable denominators and detection coverage are available
negative_expectations: No generic rewrite based only on the ambiguous trend
No deferral of a confirmed safety defect solely because it occurred once

cases.name: Experiments cannot mutate shared instructions
cases.trap: An evaluator adjusts a global skill or switches treatments during recovery
cases.prompt: A candidate SKILL.md text is stored with SHA-256 and supported by 12 comparable session trajectories. Two unrelated Sessions share the same OpenCode project location; only one is eligible and explicitly assigned to the candidate. The host exposes shared skill registry transforms and session-level instruction hooks. Determine execution and validation.
expectations: Keeps shared registry unchanged; either proves session-isolated delivery of actual candidate content or uses an isolated manual checkout
Records baseline and variant fingerprints, assignment versus actual exposure, and whole-objective outcomes
Keeps candidate fixed across retries and prevents silent promotion
negative_expectations: No shared registry toggle while unrelated Sessions run
No treatment inference from a hash alone, no promotion based on one local success
